olivia: Quick heads-up — I ran a regional cost + latency sweep for hosting 13B real-time inference (p4d/a10x equivalent). Full context: assumptions below. Summary: EU reserved capacity looks ~12% cheaper per-token vs US when amortized at 75% util, but egress and cross-region replication push net cost up ~7-9% for multi-region active-active.

olivia: Assumptions:
```
- Model: 13B, sequence avg 256 tokens
- GPU types: us-west: A100-80GB equiv (on-demand $12.5/hr, 1yr reserved effective $6.8/hr)
           eu-west: A10x equiv (on-demand $6.0/hr, 1yr reserved effective $3.1/hr)
- Utilization: 75% steady-state
- Egress: $0.09/GB within-region, $0.12/GB inter-region
- Traffic split in probe: US 55%, EU 30%, APAC 15%
- Other: KV cache hit 18%, batching avg 1.6x
```

raj: Can you share raw per-month numbers (commit cost, egress, net per-token) and how sensitive this is to util? We shouldn't trigger a big reserved commit if util drops by 10%.

olivia: Raw pareto (rough):
```
- us-west (reserve@75%): ~$0.55 / 1M tokens
- eu-west (reserve@75%): ~$0.48 / 1M tokens
- ap-southeast (on-demand mix): ~$0.72 / 1M tokens
- Inter-region replication cost add ~ $0.04-0.07 / 1M tokens depending on cross-region traffic
``` 
(Will attach full spreadsheet to the thread.)

marie: Reminder: latency SLOs matter for a bunch of EU customers — p95s we measured last week: US-west -> 28ms, EU-west -> 42ms, APAC -> 210ms. We can trade cost vs latency by routing small latency-critical traffic to local hot pools and batching long-running batched jobs in cheaper regions.

sam: Also note we have a commitment fragmentation problem: our current reserved pools are in tiny pockets across AZs. If we consolidate commits into fewer SKUs/regions we get better pricing + easier autoscale. Proposal: concentrate 1yr reserve in us-west (60%), eu-west (30%), keep apac small (10%) for coverage — keep 25% on-demand buffer for spikes.

olivia: I like that as a starting commit mix. Operational caveats: need to ensure capacity for canary and can do cross-region fallback w/o blowing egress. We should set routing policy to prefer local region, fallback to cheaper region only for batch or when TTL cached.

raj: Can infra team run a billing probe with finance: what's the delta if util falls to 60% vs 85%? And open a cloud billing ticket to validate committed discounts vs our usage patterns (billing ticket ID: CLOUD-9923).

infra-bot: Billing probe scheduled: CLOUD-9923 opened with billing team. Estimated delta: commit-savings range 12-22% depending on utilization and consolidation.

olivia: Action items:
- olivia: upload detailed spreadsheet + per-customer egress breakdown by EOD tomorrow
- raj: run util sensitivity scenarios, target 60/75/85
- sam: sketch commit consolidation plan and AZ fallbacks
- marie: define latency-tier routing rules we can implement in the routing policy

marie: +1 on timeline. let's sync Wed 10am infra/finance/product. If no objections by EOD Tue we can run a 1yr reserve quote with procurement.

sam: +1. I'll also add a note about Dedicated burst pools for tail latency — cheaper than overprovisioning in all regions.

olivia: Thanks everyone — will post spreadsheet link shortly :link: :chart_with_upwards_trend:
